title: d-Block Configurations: Why Chromium and Copper Break the Rule
subject: Chemistry
objective: The d-block's general configuration is (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻², with 4s filling before 3d. Chromium (3d⁵4s¹) and copper (3d¹⁰4s¹) move one 4s electron into 3d, because 3d and 4s are very close in energy and half-filled and full d sets are extra stable.

fill.q: The general outer configuration of the d-block is (n−1)d____ ns¹⁻².
Half-filled and completely filled d subshells are extra ____.

tf.explain: 4s is filled first in the neutral atoms of the 3d series.

tf.q: 3d and 4s orbitals are very close in energy.
tf.explain: That is why stability decides Cr and Cu.

ar.r: A half-filled d set is extra stable.
4s is always lower in energy than 3d.
ar.explain: A true; R false: 3d and 4s are very close in energy.

num.q: How many unpaired electrons does Cr (3d⁵ 4s¹) have?

short.solution: 3d and 4s are very close in energy and a completely filled d¹⁰ set is extra stable, so one 4s electron moves to 3d.
